title: Why Computers Get Hot
summary: Computers produce heat, so data centers manage airflow and temperature.
objectives: Explain why operating computers produce heat.
Describe how cooling and temperature monitoring support safe operation.

vocab.def: Systems that remove heat so equipment can operate safely.
The movement of air through and around a space.
A measure of how hot or cold something is.

sections.heading: Work creates heat
sections.body: When computers use electricity to work, some energy becomes heat. A single device may feel warm; many servers working together produce much more heat.

sections.heading: Moving heat away
sections.body: Cooling systems and airflow help carry heat away from equipment. Sensors can help people notice temperature changes before they become larger problems.

sections.heading: Observe safely
sections.body: A classroom can compare airflow around ordinary objects or use a diagram. Do not open energized equipment or touch professional cooling systems.

practice.prompt: Look at a simple room diagram and mark where cool air should enter and warm air should leave. Explain your choice.

quiz.question: What is one reason data centers need cooling?
options: Computers produce heat while they work
quiz.answer: Computers produce heat while they work

reflectionPrompt: Where have you noticed heat changing how a device works?
